$comment: The source of sf-input-textarea's element plumbing (core/js/element-manifest.js). Taken from simai/ui-control control/smart-architecture/migration/out/textarea (migration/convert-1.3.8.mjs over simai/ui-source@5100227); standard simai.smart-component 1.3.8, vocabulary 1.1.5. Every x-todo of the conversion is decided: x-decisions says how.

size.summary: The field ladder, as sf-input's (1/3, 1/2, 1, 2, 3): the text size, the side padding and the height of one row are those of sf-input of the same size.

appearance.summary: How the field looks: a bordered box, a filled one, or flush -- no box of its own, inside a composite control that draws the box and the focus.

label.summary: The visible label above the field; it names the native control. Without it, give aria-label.

required.summary: The field must hold a value: the label gets the required mark and the native control the required constraint.

placeholder.summary: Example text shown in the empty field in the quiet ink; it disappears with the first character and is not a label.

autocomplete.summary: The autofill hint the browser reads, as the native autocomplete (email, tel, current-password, off). Empty: not written.

inputmode.summary: Which on-screen keyboard a phone opens, as the native inputmode (numeric, decimal, tel, email, url, search). Empty: the keyboard of the type.

minlength.summary: The fewest characters the text may have, as the native minlength; a shorter text is invalid (too short). Unset: no limit.

maxlength.summary: The most characters the text should have (C141 (1)). The count shows from 80 % of it; past it the count and the frame turn to the error colour and the field is invalid (too-long), so the form is not sent. The text is never cut, as the native maxlength would. Unset: no limit, no count.

counter.summary: With maxlength: the count shows always, not only from 80 % of the limit (C141 (1)).

spell-check.summary: Whether the browser checks spelling in the text, as the native spellcheck. On by default; turn it off for codes and identifiers.

wrap.summary: How the text is sent: soft sends it as typed; hard also sends the line breaks the field draws at its width, as the native wrap.

text.summary: What kind of text the field holds (C141 (8)). plain: words. code: a snippet of code or configuration (a counter's script, robots.txt, JSON) -- the code font of the type system, no spelling check, no autocorrection, and the lines as typed: no wrapping, the field scrolls sideways inside. Not a code editor: no highlighting or completion.

hint.summary: The help line under the field; on an error the error message takes its place.

name.summary: The name the value is sent under in a form, as the native name.

rows.summary: How many lines a field of fixed height shows; longer text scrolls inside. Given without auto-grow it fixes the height (no growing); given with auto-grow it is the fewest rows when min-rows is not.

auto-grow.summary: The field follows its text between min-rows and max-rows and scrolls inside past max-rows (C141 (2): a form field grows from 3 to 10 rows). On unless auto-grow="false", or rows is given without auto-grow (a fixed height), or the field is flush (a composite sizes it: then it grows only with auto-grow, from 1 row and uncapped unless min-rows and max-rows say). CSS field-sizing where supported, a script fallback elsewhere.

min-rows.summary: The fewest rows a growing field shows: unset, rows when given, else 3 (a flush field 1). One row is the height of an input of the same size.

max-rows.summary: The most rows a growing field shows before it scrolls inside: unset, 10 (a flush field no cap); a value below min-rows is min-rows.

resize.summary: Draws the browser's grip that changes the height, on a field of fixed height (rows, or auto-grow="false"). Off by default (C141 (2)); never drawn on a touch screen, and a growing field has none.

disabled.summary: The field takes no input, no focus and is not sent with the form; it draws the disabled look.

readonly.summary: The value can be read, selected and copied but not changed; it is sent with the form. The field draws the region line instead of the control border.

invalid.summary: Marks the value as wrong: the error border, aria-invalid on the native control and error-message under the field.

error-message.summary: The text shown under the field while it is invalid, in the error colour, in place of the hint; it is the control's error message for assistive technology.

mask.summary: Turns on the input mask: typing is held to mask-pattern (or mask-options) and the fixed characters are drawn by the mask.

mask-pattern.summary: The mask with mask on: 0 a digit, a a letter, * any character, {...} a fixed part kept in the value, [ ] an optional tail, \ escapes the next character; any other character is shown only. Example: +{7} (000) 000-00-00.

mask-options.summary: The full mask configuration as JSON, for what mask-pattern cannot say; it wins over mask-pattern. Invalid JSON is ignored.

value.summary: The current text. Written by the page, it controls the field; the value property reads what is typed.

change.summary: The value was committed; the native event bubbles from the inner textarea, which is its target.

input.summary: The value changed while typing; the native event bubbles from the inner textarea, which is its target.

field-reset.summary: The person pressed the reset back to the inherited value. The event of the trait field-inherit@1: one name for every field of the family, so a form hears them all at once and tells them apart by detail.tag. Fired before the field is emptied and cancellable: preventDefault keeps the value. When it is not prevented the field empties, says so with its ordinary change, shows the inherited value again and takes focus back.

tag.summary: The element that was reset, as a tag name.

value.summary: The field's own value before the reset.

inherited-value.summary: The inherited value it returns to.

name.summary: The form name, empty when the field has none.

default.$comment: The Lit template in JavaScript, the migration form of §5.2 (§16): the build does not compile template.html yet, so a second copy of the markup would only drift from the one that draws.

aliases.$comment: Dated aliases of sf-input-textarea for the shim (stands/18-aliases-ci/alias.mjs, standard §16 item 20). mode: same-detail (the shim sends the new and the old name), split / detail-adds (a detail adapter, refused by the shim), attribute-and-property, method, property, manifest-only (the DOM name does not change), host-attribute (no shim), retired.

rows.note: error is a dated alias of invalid; the shim maps the attribute and the property

rows.summary: Legacy name for appearance, still honoured. See contracts/public-api-axes.json.

rows.note: the event of the trait field-inherit@1, declared in component.json as the shared event field-reset; the field sends sf-field-reset and the shim follows it with this dated name, same detail, one cancel
rows.summary: The person pressed the reset back to the inherited value. Fired before the field is emptied and cancellable: preventDefault keeps the value. When it is not prevented the field empties, says so with its ordinary change, shows the inherited value again and takes focus back.

rows.section: rename plan R0 (ui-control RENAME-PLAN-2026-11-03), naming decision 2026-11-02
rows.note: the element is sf-input-textarea; sf-textarea is a subclass defined beside it until the date

x-summary: A native multiline form control with Framework presentation, validation messaging and safe vertical resizing.
x-renamed: settings.spellcheck → spell-check: "spellcheck" is a property of HTMLElement.prototype (§3.1, §16 item 26), alias dated
x-decisions: trait-words: the field-inherit@1 words stay in lang x-trait-words beside the component words, as the sf-switch pilot keeps them; the running words are helpers/inherited-value.js INHERITED_TEXT until the trait has its own folder (Annex A item 13 is open).

trait field-inherit@1: host state data-inherited (§5.3, §20.2) and the trait event sf-field-reset with sf-field:reset as its dated same-detail alias (aliases.json), as the sf-switch pilot; an inherited value never satisfies required (§20.2).

version 1.5.0: spellcheck -> spell-check (§3.1, a property of HTMLElement), type -> appearance and error -> invalid (§17.2) are renamed members behind dated aliases, a minor (§4.10); the major comes when the aliases expire. The setting rows carry no mode: the shim maps a setting's attribute and property by kind (core/js/alias-table.js refuses a mode on a non-event row).
template: templates.default names the Lit template js/templates/default.js, the migration form §5.2 allows; no template.html until the build compiles one (a copy nothing draws would drift).
examples: examples.json from studio.fixture.json (the required comment reference) plus filled, flush, auto-grow, invalid, disabled, read-only, inherited and size 2.
css-variables: the six public variables of public-variables.v1.json plus --sf-textarea-invalid-border-color for the invalid state (§6).
form.validity: what the native textarea reports and the host mirrors -- value-missing, too-short, too-long -- and custom-error (§17.2).
form: the host is the form control through ElementInternals; the textarea carries no name (§17.1 item 6); read-only still submits.
accessibility.name: the visible label, else the host's aria-label; the host's aria-labelledby always (version 1.7.1, simai/ui-source#30).

version 1.5.1: the first-paint snapshots are retaken: the JSON island is printed once (no held copy), the icon font's state (sf-icon loaded, sf-icon-loaded) is left out, a closed surface prints closed and a size or place the code measured (a non-zero px width, height, inset, clip or transform) is left out, so a snapshot is the same on every run.

version 1.5.2: the bundle carries no element layer of its own -- element-manifest, aliases, the alias table, the host port, deprecations, page actions, the layer stack, the open-surface mark and the instance path come from the page's shared runtime (SF.runtimeModule, runtime ABI 1, core.runtime 1.1.0), one instance per page -- and embeds of this file only the keys the runtime reads. Behaviour unchanged.

version 1.6.0: the trait event is declared in component.json as the shared event field-reset (standard 1.3.13 §8: an event a trait brings is named sf-<verb>, with no tag): the element sends sf-field-reset itself and the manifest describes it, with tag in the detail. Before, the registry described only the retired sf-field:reset and no current name, and the new name came from the alias shim alone. The dated sf-field:reset follows with the same detail and one cancel until 2026-12-01.

version 1.7.0: the tag is sf-input-textarea (naming decision 2026-11-02: sf-[set]-<block>[-<variant>]); the folder, the id smart.input-textarea and the bundle cl-input-textarea follow it. sf-textarea stays a dated alias until 2027-01-01: a subclass the Smart base defines beside the new tag, listed in the rule, in sheets as :is(sf-input-textarea, sf-textarea) (change journal tag-sf-textarea-to-sf-input-textarea, path-smart-textarea-to-input-textarea).

version 1.7.1: the host's aria-label and aria-labelledby reach the native textarea, as sf-input's aria-label does (simai/ui-source#30): a textarea with no visible label -- a flush field in a card, a record panel that prints the label beside it -- was unnamed to assistive technology, because the host is not the control. A visible label still names it through the wrapping <label>, and wins over aria-label; aria-labelledby is the author's explicit choice and always lands. Both are read by the element, never settings (§3.1).

version 1.7.2: with a hint or an error and an inherited value, the inherited sentence is also a hidden note that aria-describedby names after the message, because a browser reads aria-describedby instead of aria-description and the sentence went unsaid (helpers/inherited-value.js, syncInheritedNote). Nothing is drawn differently.

version 1.7.3 (2026-11-08): a patch, nothing drawn differently by this element. Its shared helper src/smart/helpers/inherited-value.js changed with the actions block (module.smart-helpers 1.3.0). Settings, values, events and keys unchanged.

version 1.7.4 (2026-11-09): a patch; nothing in the component changed. A shared sheet it draws with moved in the next block (src/smart/helpers/inherited-value.css, the C27 inherited-value reset), so the component takes a patch with it.

version 1.7.5 (2026-11-10): a patch (TA-07, DEV precheck forms A). Every setting has its words: the 20 settings and the value that had none (size, label, required, placeholder, autocomplete, inputmode, minlength, maxlength, spell-check, wrap, hint, name, rows, disabled, readonly, invalid, error-message, mask, mask-pattern, mask-options, value) say what they do in the reference. The class sheet it draws with (component.textarea 1.1.1, FA-08) keeps a filled field's placeholder on the quiet ink, on-surface-variant; only the text is on-surface.

version 1.8.0 (2026-11-11): a minor (C55 acceptance F1: one form reads as one). A required field left empty shows its required error once the form's check fails -- the host's invalid event on a submit attempt, checkValidity() or reportValidity() -- as sf-dropdown 1.9.0 does: the error border (filled: the error fill), «Заполните поле» (lang runtime value-missing; en «Fill in this field») under the field in the field-message type, aria-invalid and aria-errormessage on the control; the person's input that fills it, or form.reset(), clears it. Before, only the browser's bubble said it. The bubble and the browser's focus on the first invalid field are unchanged; the page's invalid and error-message win over it (helpers/form-field.js ShownRequired). R2 (DEV acceptance 2026-11-11, D1): the shown required error goes whenever the value stops being missing, whatever set it -- the person's input or change, a value set from script, a value attribute -- as sf-dropdown 1.9.0 (ShownRequired clears in the form sync every one of them ends in, not on input/change only). D2: form.reset() puts back the declared value (the value attribute), never the live text: the template bound .defaultValue to the current value, so the render that cleared the error on the first keystroke made that character the default and reset kept it (FormData sent it).

version 1.9.0 (2026-11-14, fields ladder; study control/research/2026-11-14-textarea-rich-text.md TR-2): a minor. size takes the field ladder's five steps, 1/3, 1/2, 1, 2, 3, as sf-input and the six fields of the fields ladder: at 1/3 and 3 one row is 28 / 56 high at 1440 (24 / 48 compact, 24 / 52 on a phone), the text the step's, the label, hint and error a step below, the value where sf-input's starts at those steps (19 / 37 from the outer edge at 1440); it drew 1/3 and 3 at 1/2 and 2 with a console note (component.textarea 1.4.0 no longer retires the size class). On a touch phone, where the core lifts the text to 16px, the lines stand on at least the size-1 line (20px): a 1/2 field drew 16px text on 16px lines and its lines touched; a fixed one-row field keeps its control height. 1/2, 1 and 2 on a desktop unchanged; settings, values, events and keys unchanged. Owner decision C141 (2026-11-14; study TR-4, TR-5, #q-code) in the same minor: (1) maxlength no longer reaches the native textarea, which cut a paste; the field counts the text itself with the shared rule of src/smart/helpers/char-count.js (sf-chat-composer's): the count stands at the end of the message line from 80 % of the limit (always with the new counter), and past the limit the count and the frame are the error colour and the host is invalid (too-long, the word too-long), so the form is not sent; the text is kept whole; a polite line speaks a threshold once. (2) A form field grows with its text from 3 to 10 rows by default (auto-grow on, min-rows 3, max-rows 10); rows given without auto-grow keeps a fixed height, and flush keeps its old behaviour (grows only with auto-grow, from 1 row, uncapped); the browser's grip is gone unless the new resize asks for it on a fixed field, and is never drawn on a touch screen (component.textarea 1.4.0). (8) text="code": the type system's code font, spell-check off, no autocorrection, no wrapping (the field scrolls sideways); text is the setting's name because it says what kind of text the field holds, as inputmode says which keyboard, and leaves «code» alone to sf-input-code (one-time codes).

ai_guidance.use_when: Use sf-input-textarea for comments, descriptions and other free text that may contain multiple lines and must participate in a native form.
do_not: Do not use Textarea for short single-line values, rich text or code editing
Do not enable horizontal resizing inside responsive layouts without an explicit layout decision
Do not put Enter-to-send into the textarea: in a form Enter is a newline; a chat composer handles it itself
Do not copy generated ui-smart code
Do not move host data or access decisions into the component

accessibility.focus: Keep visible focus on the active control. After a reset back to the inherited value, focus returns to the control; while the value is inherited, the control carries it as aria-description and the visible marker is aria-hidden.

sf-field:reset.summary: The person pressed the reset back to the inherited value. Fired before the field is emptied and cancellable: preventDefault keeps the value. When it is not prevented the field empties, says so with its ordinary change, shows the inherited value again and takes focus back.

value.description: The field's own value before the reset.

inheritedValue.description: The inherited value it returns to.

name.description: The form name, empty when the field has none.

setState.summary: Applies disabled, error or invalid, errorMessage and value to the inner textarea and resyncs its field semantics; setting value dispatches input. Returns false when the textarea is not rendered.

resetToInherited.summary: Returns the field to its inherited value, as the reset button does: fires the cancellable sf-field-reset, then empties the own value and focuses the control. Returns whether it was reset (false without an inherited value, without an own value, while disabled or readonly, or when the event was prevented).

aria-label.description: Accessible name for a textarea drawn without a visible label; it lands on the native textarea. A visible label wins.

aria-labelledby.description: Ids of the elements that name the textarea; it lands on the native textarea.

inherited-value.description: What the field falls back to while it holds no value of its own. Shown as inherited, in the placeholder's ink with an «inherited» marker under the field, never as the value: the form value stays empty. Once the field holds a value of its own, a reset button returns it here.

inherited-text.description: The words of the marker shown while the inherited value applies. Unset, it follows the page's language («inherited», «наследуется»).

reset-label.description: The accessible name of the button that returns the field to the inherited value. Unset, it follows the page's language («Reset to inherited», «Сбросить к наследуемому»).
